latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Anti-U1-RNP-associated immune complexes and RNA-containing autoantigens activate endosomal TLR and type I interferon pathways, creating the central autoimmune manifold.
BAFF-supported B-cell activation produces high ANA, anti-RNP, anti-Sm/RNP, anti-SSA/Ro, and overlap autoantibody patterns, with variable complement consumption and cytopenias.
Endothelial injury and small-vessel remodeling produce Raynaud phenomenon, puffy hands, sclerodactyly, digital ulcers or gangrene, renal-crisis-like hypertension, and pulmonary vascular disease.
RA-like or lupus-like immune synovitis drives arthralgia, polyarthritis, morning stiffness, synovitis, and functional pain.
Polymyositis-like inflammatory muscle injury produces proximal weakness, myalgia, dysphagia, CK/myoglobin/LDH/transaminase release, and rarely rhabdomyolysis-AKI physiology.
CTD-associated NSIP/OP/UIP-like inflammatory and fibrosing lung injury creates ground glass, reticulation, traction bronchiectasis, restriction, DLCO decline, dyspnea, and hypoxemia.
Precapillary pulmonary vascular remodeling can emerge with or without ILD and drives elevated pulmonary pressures, RV strain, exertional dyspnea, syncope risk, and right-heart failure.
Immune-complex and endothelial inflammation produces fever, rash, alopecia, pleuritis, pericarditis, pleural or pericardial effusions, and inflammatory chest pain.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Renal, TMA, and immune-complex rare pathway
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: A minority of MCTD courses develop proteinuria, renal-crisis-like hypertension, immune-complex kidney injury, thrombotic microangiopathy, or TTP-like ADAMTS13 autoimmunity.
Cytokine and acute-phase activity creates fatigue, fever, weight loss, anemia of inflammation, ESR/CRP elevation, hypoalbuminemia, and flare-related constitutional burden.

Innate immune activation raises acute-phase and constitutional inflammatory activity.
Anti-RNP reactivity is the serologic anchor of the manifold.

High ANA reciprocal titers support the autoimmune manifold.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Anti-U1-RNP-positive MCTD usually sits in an ANA-positive serologic state.
More severe or persistent Raynaud raises digital ulcer risk.
Ulcers can progress to gangrene when perfusion is critically impaired.
CK and weakness usually track inflammatory myositis but can be discordant.
More extensive ILD can lower oxygen saturation.
ILD burden commonly reduces diffusion capacity.
Pulmonary hypertension can raise RV wall stress and natriuretic peptides.
Progressive PAH raises right-heart failure hazard.
Pleural or pericardial inflammation causes pleuritic or positional pain.
Pericardial inflammation may coincide with mild myocardial injury.
Severe thrombocytopenia with hemolysis raises TMA/TTP hazard.
MCTD-associated TTP/TMA can be rapidly fatal.
Right-heart failure is a major PAH outcome driver.
Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure increases short-term mortality risk.

treatments.clinical_role: Rapid suppression of inflammatory arthritis, serositis, rash, fever, and myositis; dose depends on organ threat.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: Glucocorticoids suppress broad inflammatory activity.
Serositis and cutaneous inflammation often respond quickly.
Steroids reduce inflammatory muscle injury and CK over days to weeks.
Dose-dependent immunosuppression increases infection risk.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Untreated infection changes the risk-benefit balance of immunosuppression.
High-dose steroids can worsen hypertension and renal-crisis-like physiology.

treatments.clinical_role: Chronic control of arthralgia, arthritis, rash, fatigue, and flare tendency in lupus-like MCTD activity.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: Antimalarial immunomodulation dampens endosomal TLR signaling.
Joint and skin symptoms may improve gradually.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Renal disease, high cumulative dose, or long exposure increases retinal monitoring need.

treatments.clinical_role: Steroid-sparing immune control for ILD, serocutaneous overlap, or renal immune activity.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: MMF reduces lymphocyte-driven CTD-ILD inflammation and can stabilize lung trajectory.
Antimetabolite therapy suppresses lymphocyte proliferation.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: MMF is teratogenic and must be replaced before conception.
Additional immunosuppression increases infection risk.

treatments.clinical_role: Maintenance or steroid-sparing therapy for joint, skin, serositis, myositis, or pregnancy-compatible immune control.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: Azathioprine can maintain inflammatory myositis control.
Helps sustain remission in lupus-like manifestations.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Deficient metabolism increases myelosuppression risk.

treatments.clinical_role: Steroid-sparing control of inflammatory arthritis and selected myositis-predominant courses when lung and renal context permit.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: Methotrexate reduces inflammatory synovitis.
Can help chronic inflammatory myositis in selected patients.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Significant ILD shifts treatment selection toward lung-directed agents.
Renal dysfunction increases methotrexate toxicity.

treatments.clinical_role: Escalation for organ-threatening ILD, CNS disease, renal immune injury, myocarditis, or severe vasculitic overlap.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: Cyclophosphamide can suppress severe inflammatory CTD-ILD.
May suppress severe immune-complex or vasculitic renal activity, but does not replace urgent TTP-directed therapy.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Cumulative gonadal toxicity affects treatment planning.
Profound immunosuppression increases infection risk.

treatments.clinical_role: B-cell depletion for refractory arthritis, cytopenias, severe overlap activity, or selected ILD/myositis courses.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: CD20 B-cell depletion lowers autoantibody-generating activity over weeks.
Refractory inflammatory arthritis can respond as B-cell activity falls.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: HBV screening and prophylaxis are required when risk is present.

treatments.clinical_role: Adjunct for severe myositis, immune cytopenia, or when infection risk constrains deeper immunosuppression.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: IVIG can reduce immune myositis activity and improve strength in selected courses.
Can improve immune thrombocytopenia physiology, but TTP still requires TTP-directed treatment.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: IVIG can increase viscosity and thrombotic risk.
Renal dysfunction raises infusion and product-selection risk.

treatments.clinical_role: Antifibrotic vector for progressive fibrosing ILD phenotype, complementary to immune control when fibrosis dominates.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: Nintedanib slows fibrosing ILD progression rather than rapidly reversing inflammation.
Slows architectural fibrotic progression.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Liver injury increases antifibrotic toxicity concerns.
VEGFR inhibition can affect bleeding risk.

treatments.clinical_role: Pulmonary vasodilator support for precapillary pulmonary hypertension, improving pulmonary vascular resistance and RV load.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: Sildenafil or tadalafil can lower pulmonary vascular tone.
Reduced pulmonary vascular resistance can lower RV failure hazard.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Concomitant nitrates can cause severe hypotension.

treatments.display_name: Endothelin receptor antagonist for pulmonary hypertension
treatments.clinical_role: Pulmonary vascular remodeling and vasoconstriction modulation in confirmed PAH context.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: Endothelin blockade reduces pulmonary vascular constriction/remodeling signaling.
Lower PAH burden reduces RV failure trajectory.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Endothelin antagonists are teratogenic.
Hepatotoxicity monitoring is important.

treatments.display_name: Prostacyclin pathway therapy for pulmonary hypertension
treatments.clinical_role: Escalated pulmonary vasodilator support for high-risk PAH or RV failure physiology.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: Prostacyclin analogs or receptor agonists reduce pulmonary vascular resistance.
Unloading RV pressure stress can improve PAH hazard trajectory.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Parenteral prostacyclin routes can add catheter infection risk.

treatments.display_name: ACE inhibitor and calcium-channel blocker for vascular/renal context
treatments.clinical_role: Blood-pressure and vasospasm control when severe hypertension, renal-crisis-like physiology, or Raynaud/digital ischemia is present.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: Captopril/nifedipine can lower severe hypertension.
Calcium-channel blockade reduces vasospasm.
ACE inhibition is a core vector for renal-crisis-like hypertension physiology.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: ACE inhibition can worsen hyperkalemia.
Vasodilators can worsen hypotension.

treatments.clinical_role: Urgent TTP/TMA-directed intervention when MCTD course expresses severe thrombocytopenia, hemolysis, neurologic/renal/cardiac injury, and ADAMTS13 inhibitor context.

trajectory_modifications.clinical_rationale: Plasma exchange removes inhibitory antibodies and replenishes ADAMTS13 when immune TTP physiology is present.
Effective TTP treatment allows platelet recovery.
Microangiopathic hemolysis should fall if TTP physiology is controlled.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Severe ADAMTS13 deficiency and inhibitor positivity increase TTP-targeted benefit.
Apheresis catheter placement and coagulopathy add procedure risk.

modulation.clinical_rationale: MCTD is more common in women.
Ro52/SSA positivity is associated with more lung involvement in several CTD overlap settings.
PL-7, Jo-1, or related antibodies can amplify ILD/myositis expression without changing the first-layer disease name.
SSc-like vasculopathy increases digital, pulmonary vascular, and renal-crisis-like expression.
Baseline ILD lowers reserve and raises pulmonary hazard.
PAH is a major prognostic branch in MCTD.
Reflux and aspiration can worsen cough, dyspnea, and lung injury context.
Severe hypertension and renal vascular injury amplify renal-risk axes.
Infection can trigger or mimic flare and changes steroid/immunosuppression toxicity.
Pregnancy changes acceptable immunosuppressive and PAH vectors.
Longstanding inflammation can promote organ damage and rare amyloid/cardiac complications.

supportive_care.clinical_role: Serial PFT including DLCO and HRCT when symptoms, crackles, or known ILD are present; maps ILD extent, fibrosis, and response trajectory.
Echocardiography, NT-proBNP, DLCO trend, and right-heart catheterization when PAH is suspected; distinguishes PAH from ILD, left-heart, thromboembolic, or anemia contexts.
Cold avoidance, smoking cessation, vasodilator titration, wound care, and ischemia surveillance for ulcers or gangrene.
Trend CK, strength, dysphagia/aspiration risk, physical therapy, fall prevention, and respiratory muscle monitoring in severe weakness.
Urinalysis, creatinine, blood pressure, CBC, smear, LDH, haptoglobin, and ADAMTS13 testing when thrombocytopenia or hemolysis appears.
ECG, troponin, echocardiography, and chest imaging for pleuritic or positional chest pain, effusions, dyspnea, or heart-failure signs.
Cultures, viral testing, imaging, and BAL when pulmonary infiltrates or fever could be infectious before intensifying immune suppression.
Vaccination review, hepatitis/TB screening for biologics, and PJP prophylaxis when high-dose or multi-agent immunosuppression creates sufficient risk.
CBC, liver enzymes, renal function, pregnancy testing where relevant, eye screening for hydroxychloroquine, and fertility counseling for cyclophosphamide exposure.
Rheumatology plus pulmonology, cardiology/PAH, nephrology, neurology, dermatology, and rehabilitation as organ axes emerge.
